stem: If the line \(\frac{x}{3}=\frac{y}{4}=z\) is perpendicular to the line \(\frac{x-1}{k}=\frac{y+2}{3}=\frac{z-3}{k-1}\) then the value of \(k\) is:
solution: Direction ratios of the lines are \((3,4,1)\) and \((k,3,k-1)\). Perpendicularity: \(3k+12+(k-1)=0\Rightarrow 4k+11=0\Rightarrow k=-\frac{11}{4}\).

stem: The vector equation of line \(2x-1=3y+2=z-2\) is
solution: Setting \(2x-1=3y+2=z-2=t\): \(x=\frac{t+1}{2},\ y=\frac{t-2}{3},\ z=t+2\). Symmetric form \(\frac{x-1/2}{1/2}=\frac{y+2/3}{1/3}=\frac{z-2}{1}\), so a point is \((\tfrac12,-\tfrac23,2)\) and direction ratios \((3,2,6)\). Hence \(\bar{r}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\hat{i}-\frac{2}{3}\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\right)+\lambda\left(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\right)\).

stem: The length of the perpendicular from \((1,6,3)\) to the line \(\frac{x}{1}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z-2}{3}\)
solution: A general point is \((t,1+2t,2+3t)\). The vector from \((1,6,3)\) is \((t-1,2t-5,3t-1)\); setting its dot with \((1,2,3)\) to \(0\) gives \(14t-14=0\Rightarrow t=1\), foot \((1,3,5)\). Distance \(=\sqrt{0+9+4}=\sqrt{13}\).

stem: The shortest distance between the lines \(\bar{r}=\left(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)+\lambda\left(\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}\right)\) and \(\bar{r}=\left(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}\right)+\mu\left(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\right)\) is
solution: MISPRINT (book options appear defective). \(\bar{b}_1\times\bar{b}_2=(1,-1,-1)\times(2,1,2)=(-1,-4,3)\), \(|\bar{b}_1\times\bar{b}_2|=\sqrt{26}\). With \(\bar{a}_2-\bar{a}_1=(1,-3,-2)\), \((\bar{a}_2-\bar{a}_1)\cdot(\bar{b}_1\times\bar{b}_2)=-1+12-6=5\), so shortest distance \(=\frac{5}{\sqrt{26}}\), which matches none of the printed options — needs downstream verification of the intended line vectors.

stem: The lines \(\frac{x-2}{1}=\frac{y-3}{1}=\frac{z-4}{-k}\) and \(\frac{x-1}{k}=\frac{y-4}{2}=\frac{z-5}{1}\) are coplanar if
solution: With points \((2,3,4),(1,4,5)\), difference \((-1,1,1)\), and directions \((1,1,-k),(k,2,1)\), the coplanarity determinant \(\begin{vmatrix}-1&1&1\\1&1&-k\\k&2&1\end{vmatrix}=-k^2-3k=0\Rightarrow k(k+3)=0\Rightarrow k=0\) or \(-3\).

stem: The lines \(\frac{x}{1}=\frac{y}{2}=\frac{z}{3}\) and \(\frac{x-1}{-2}=\frac{y-2}{-4}=\frac{z-3}{6}\) are
solution: Directions \((1,2,3)\) and \((-2,-4,6)\) are neither proportional (not parallel) nor perpendicular (dot \(=8\ne0\)). The coplanarity determinant with rows \((1,2,3),(1,2,3),(-2,-4,6)\) has two equal rows, so it is \(0\); hence the lines are coplanar and, being non-parallel, intersecting.

stem: The angle between the lines \(2x=3y=-z\) and \(6x=-y=-4z\) is
solution: Direction ratios are \((3,2,-6)\) and \((2,-12,-3)\); their dot product \(6-24+18=0\), so the lines are perpendicular, angle \(90^\circ\).

stem: The direction ratios of the line \(3x+1=6y-2=1-z\) are
solution: Setting \(3x+1=6y-2=1-z=t\): \(x=\frac{t-1}{3},\ y=\frac{t+2}{6},\ z=1-t\), so direction ratios \(\left(\frac13,\frac16,-1\right)\propto(2,1,-6)\).

stem: The perpendicular distance of the plane \(2x+3y-z=k\) from the origin is \(\sqrt{14}\) units, the value of \(k\) is
solution: Distance \(=\frac{|k|}{\sqrt{4+9+1}}=\frac{|k|}{\sqrt{14}}=\sqrt{14}\Rightarrow |k|=14\).

subtopic: Angle Between Planes and Line-Plane Angle
stem: The angle between the planes \(\bar{r}\cdot\left(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\right)+4=0\) and \(\bar{r}\cdot\left(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\right)+7=0\) is
solution: With normals \((1,-2,3)\) and \((2,1,-3)\), \(\cos\theta=\frac{|2-2-9|}{\sqrt{14}\cdot\sqrt{14}}=\frac{9}{14}\), so \(\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{9}{14}\right)\).

stem: If the planes \(\bar{r}\cdot\left(2\hat{i}-\lambda\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)=3\) and \(\bar{r}\cdot\left(4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\mu\hat{k}\right)=5\) are parallel, then the values of \(\lambda\) and \(\mu\) are respectively.
solution: Parallel planes have proportional normals: \(\frac{2}{4}=\frac{-\lambda}{-1}=\frac{1}{\mu}\). Thus \(\lambda=\frac{1}{2}\) and \(\mu=2\).

stem: The equation of the plane passing through \((2,-1,3)\) and making equal intercepts on the coordinate axes is
solution: Equal intercepts give \(x+y+z=a\). Through \((2,-1,3)\): \(a=2-1+3=4\), so \(x+y+z=4\).

stem: Measure of angle between the planes \(5x-2y+3z-7=0\) and \(15x-6y+9z+5=0\) is
solution: The normal \((15,-6,9)=3(5,-2,3)\) is parallel to \((5,-2,3)\), so the planes are parallel and the angle between them is \(0^\circ\).

stem: The direction cosines of the normal to the plane \(2x-y+2z=3\) are
solution: Normal \((2,-1,2)\) has magnitude \(3\); direction cosines \(\left(\frac{2}{3},-\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}\right)\).

stem: The equation of the plane passing through the points \((1,-1,1)\), \((3,2,4)\) and parallel to Y-axis is:
solution: Parallel to Y-axis means the plane has form \(ax+cz+d=0\). Through \((1,-1,1)\): \(a+c+d=0\); through \((3,2,4)\): \(3a+4c+d=0\). Subtracting, \(2a+3c=0\Rightarrow a=-\frac{3c}{2}\); take \(c=2,a=-3,d=1\), giving \(-3x+2z+1=0\), i.e. \(3x-2z=1\).

stem: If the line \(\frac{x+1}{2}=\frac{y-m}{3}=\frac{z-4}{6}\) lies in the plane \(3x-14y+6z+49=0\), then the value of \(m\) is:
solution: The point \((-1,m,4)\) must lie in the plane: \(3(-1)-14m+6(4)+49=0\Rightarrow 70-14m=0\Rightarrow m=5\) (the direction \((2,3,6)\) also satisfies \(2\cdot3+3(-14)+6\cdot6=0\)).
